# WS-D — BC-P2-37: a trust report taken from an unauthenticated release field  (MEDIUM; blocks AC-3)

## The defect, exactly
`gov update` decides "already up to date" from the candidate source's own declared version — read from its
`KERNEL.yaml` / `KERNEL_MANIFEST.json` — **before** the single verification policy runs
(`runtime/src/update.rs` around lines 238-240 and 55-63). A payload-tampered source, a foreign-signed source and a
correctly-signed-but-below-floor source each return `{"ok": true, "applied": false, "reason": "already up to date"}`.
Nothing installs, so this is a false clearance rather than an admission — but it is an affirmative trust report about a
source whose authenticity was never established. Verifier finding `V1-S5-01` (alpha), confirmed blocking by the synthesis
verifier because Contract v3:154 makes "tampered source payload … altered security policy" A2's own advanced-qualification
challenge.

## What must become true
`gov update` must not return an affirmative result about a source whose authenticity it has not established. Either the
source is authenticated before any conclusion is drawn from its declared identity, or the result states plainly that the
source was not authenticated and makes no currency claim about it.

## Normative sources (quoted)
- Contract v3:937 — S5's bullet "authenticated source".
- Contract v3:143 — "Release/source authenticity is established before any privileged kernel material is staged or
  installed."
- Contract v3:148 — "Source-release authentication detects pre-install tampering."
- OD-P2-02 stays in force: on an unprovisioned machine, external-source kernel ingress is refused before staging, and the
  embedded bootstrap payload remains available and marked uncertified. Do not break that path.

## Acceptance evidence a later verifier will demand
Three sources at the installed version string — payload-tampered, foreign-signed, and correctly signed but below the
machine's floor — each produce a typed, non-affirmative result from `gov update --apply` and from `--check`; and a
correctly signed at-version source still reports "up to date" as it should.

## Files you own
`runtime/src/update.rs`, and new tests in `tests/certification/r2_wsd.rs` plus its `mod` line.

## Integration surface
The verification policy and the staging path are `runtime/src/srr/**` — R1-frozen territory you must not edit. Call the
existing verifier; do not reimplement or bypass it. If the only correct fix needs a change under `srr/`, stop that item and
say so precisely in your result: that is an R1 surface and needs an independent decision.

## Mutation scope
`update.rs` and your test file only.

## Checks available
`build`, `fmt`, `lib_tests`, `cert_wsd`, `cert_update` (existing update/kernel certification tests that must not regress),
`update_tests` (update unit tests).
